Subject: Conversation waterfall: intermittent streaming pacing regression & immediate mitigations

Hi Anna —

Quick heads-up: our telemetry picked up an intermittent increase in tail latency for streaming/chat endpoints starting ~08:45 PDT. The pattern looks like a "conversation waterfall" where long-context requests are delivered in uneven token bursts (small tokens, then a pause, then a chunk), which many UIs surface as stuttering or short freezes.

What we're seeing (summary):
- Affected endpoints: /v1/streams and the chat streaming path for models with >8k context in a single session.
- Tail latency spikes only during high token-cadence conversations and when prefix/KV warmups are used heavily. Spikes are ~300–700ms additional per-chunk in affected windows.
- Not all regions affected; current spike is in us-west-2 edge pool.

Immediate mitigations you can try (client/playbook):
1) Temporarily reduce max_tokens_per_chunk to 64 (default 256) — evens out chunk sizes and lowers per-chunk processing time.
2) Add a 200–400ms jitter buffer on the client UI to smooth visual presentation while we stabilize the stream.
3) If possible, enable the non-streaming fallback (polling-style) for high-throughput sessions until we confirm the rollout; we can help script the fallback.
4) Add a short prefix request (1 token warmup) for long-context sessions to reduce KV warmup variability.

Attached: clearstream_incident_snapshot_0606.json (short telemetry capture we pulled from your session ids you sent earlier) and a concise mitigation checklist.

We're actively triaging; Marcus is leading the runtime investigation and Ben is preparing an ops plan for prioritized routing if needed. Would you be able to share a couple of session ids (one affected, one nominal) and a short recording of the UI freeze? That will help us correlate trace ids.

Apologies for the interruption — we will keep you updated as we make progress and will follow up with a short post-incident summary once we have root cause.

Best,
Stephanie Nguyen

Anna —

Short update with actions we've applied and next steps:

What we found (summary):
- Root cause: a scheduling regression in the serving runtime scheduler introduced in yesterday's scheduler tuning. The regression caused uneven batching behavior for long-context streaming requests (the runtime would occasionally group large KV-prefixed sessions into a single micro-batch then wait for an extra scheduling tick, producing the waterfall pattern).
- Scope: isolated to a subset of us-west-2 edge nodes; only sessions with sustained high token cadence and heavy KV prefix usage were affected.

Actions taken (what we did):
1) Deployed an incremental hotfix at 13:05 PDT that forces deterministic bin-splitting for long-context streaming requests (this removes the extra wait tick).
2) Applied a priority route for ClearStream traffic between 12:40–14:30 PDT as a precaution.
3) Enabled an expedited kernel fallback on affected nodes while we fully validate the hotfix.

Customer-visible result: tail chunk latency dropped to baseline within ~25 minutes after the hotfix; we monitored your session ids (session_20280606_cs_77) and saw the chunk gaps close and UI rendering smooth out. If you re-enable streaming now you should see normal behavior; if you'd rather we can coordinate a test window.

Compensation & follow-up:
- We're preparing a short post-incident summary with timelines and a permanent remediation plan (root cause and long-term fix) — expect that by EOD tomorrow.
- We're also preparing a goodwill credit for the impacted window (we'll propose a 10% usage credit for the hour of peak impact unless you prefer a different arrangement).

Attachments: mitigation_playbook_v1.pdf (checklist for re-enabling streaming safely), clearstream_incident_snapshot_0606.json (telemetry snippet we pulled).

Immediate asks from you:
- Can you re-enable streaming for a small test cohort (10 users) and reply here with whether you see any residual stutter?
- If you have video captures of the UI freeze, please forward them to support@clearstream.io — they help correlate client render timing with server traces.

Sorry again for the disruption. Marcus will send the internal RCA and runbook for your engineering team tomorrow, and Ben will follow up on credits and status messaging.
